title: Unix Timestamp Converter
description: Convert Unix timestamp to date and date to timestamp, with UTC, local time, seconds, and milliseconds.
metaDescription: Convert Unix timestamp to date and date to timestamp, with UTC, local time, seconds, and milliseconds.

form.title: Convert timestamp
form.description: Turn Unix values into readable dates or generate timestamps from a date and time.

mode.title: Conversion mode
mode.privacy: The conversion runs in the browser. Shared values appear only in the generated URL.

timestamp.title: Unix timestamp
timestamp.description: Paste a value in seconds or milliseconds.
timestamp.label: Timestamp value
timestamp.hint: Seconds accept up to 3 decimal places. Milliseconds must be integers.

date.title: Date and time
date.description: Enter a real date and a 24-hour time.

zone.title: Date interpretation
zone.hint: UTC is deterministic. Local uses this browser's timezone.

share.title: Share
share.description: The link uses only the visible, normalized values on this screen.
share.safe: UTC and Unix timestamps reopen the same instant on another device.
share.localWarning: Local-time links may be interpreted in another device's local timezone.

result.title: Result
result.description: Compare seconds, milliseconds, ISO UTC, and the local display.
result.emptyDescription: Enter a timestamp to see the matching date.

issues.invalidTimestampFormat: Use only numbers, an optional leading minus sign, and a decimal point when the unit is seconds.
issues.tooManyFractionDigits: Fractional seconds accept at most 3 decimal places.
issues.millisecondsMustBeInteger: Millisecond timestamps must be whole numbers.
issues.timestampOutOfRange: The value is outside the JavaScript Date range.
issues.invalidDateFormat: Use a date in YYYY-MM-DD format.
issues.invalidDateValue: The entered date does not exist in the Gregorian calendar.
issues.invalidTimeFormat: Use time as HH:mm, HH:mm:ss, or HH:mm:ss.SSS.
issues.invalidLocalTime: This local time does not exist in this timezone, possibly because of a clock change.

javascript.title: JavaScript uses milliseconds
javascript.description: Date works with milliseconds; the tool also shows the seconds version.

timezone.title: UTC and local
timezone.description: UTC represents the stable instant. Local date depends on the timezone configured in the browser.

limits.title: Limits
limits.description: Conversion follows the ECMAScript Date range and does not model leap seconds.

definition.question: What is a Unix timestamp?
definition.answer: It is a number that represents time counted from 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z, usually in seconds.

units.question: Does Unix timestamp use seconds or milliseconds?
units.answer: Unix systems commonly use seconds. JavaScript APIs and many logs use milliseconds.

utcLocal.question: What is the difference between UTC and local time?
utcLocal.answer: UTC is the global reference for the instant. Local time is how that instant appears in the browser timezone.

differentComputer.question: Why does the same timestamp show another time?
differentComputer.answer: The instant is the same, but computers in different timezones show different local times.

leapSeconds.question: Does the converter handle leap seconds?
leapSeconds.answer: No. JavaScript Date and common Unix timestamps use POSIX-style counting without a leap-second table.

before1970.question: Can I convert dates before 1970?
before1970.answer: Yes. They appear as negative timestamps when they are inside the accepted Date range.

seo.about: The converter turns Unix timestamps into UTC and local dates, and also calculates Unix seconds and milliseconds from a date. Values are processed in the browser, and shared links include the visible data in the URL.
seo.howToUse: Choose timestamp to date or date to timestamp. Use UTC for a deterministic result across devices; use local time only when the input is a browser wall-clock time.
